title: bug: CI never runs scripts/tests/local-runner-guard.test.mjs (G1-G9), so the root GUARD PID-namespace containment has no CI coverage
description: a4a729dd (b0734674) added local-runner-guard.test.mjs, but .github/workflows/ci.yml's "Test local runner prerequisite bundles" line at ca2532d5 lists 11 local-runner files and not this one. Evidence: on WSL (unprivileged user namespaces allowed) `env -i … node --test scripts/tests/local-runner-guard.test.mjs` gives 9 tests, 9 pass, 0 skip (CQ-R13 gate, 2026-10-31). Add it to that line. Decide whether CI must refuse the root rows' skip (they skip where unprivileged user namespaces are refused, e.g. AppArmor's restriction on ubuntu-24.04 runners); comment-c0616446 on task-f4811a72 suggested `grep -x '# skipped 0'` as the a4a7 gate does. ci.yml only: no supervisor or test change.
definitionOfDone: ci.yml's local-runner line runs scripts/tests/local-runner-guard.test.mjs on every OS in its matrix.
The PR's CI run shows G1-G9 executed (or a deliberate, documented skip policy for hosts that refuse unprivileged user namespaces).
No change to scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py or any test file.

implementationPlan.description:
.github/workflows/ci.yml only (DoD 1, DoD 2). Write it with the Edit tool only. Several open rows declare ci.yml (fa7fece5, 3ad573a7, f6228433, 4fdc7590, 0921d6d7, 4e412148), and a shell write leaves no TOOL witness, so landing would hold the path. Never touch scripts/local-runner/guest-supervisor.py or any test file (DoD 3, task rail: CQ-R13's certified supervisorSha256 must not move).

0. Read `git diff HEAD -- .github/workflows/ci.yml`. Any uncommitted hunk there belongs to a peer: keep its bytes and name it in the step note.

1. RED. From the repo root, run step 2's structural check against the unedited file. Copy it verbatim: from `python3 -I -c '` through `print("CI_GUARD_STEPS_OK")'`, followed by the argument /tmp/25d76cd5-red.gate.sh. Expect an AssertionError naming the 'Test local runner prerequisite bundles' step, exit 1, because the guard file is not on the line yet. Quote it in the step note.

2. Edit A. In job build-all-platforms, append ` scripts/tests/local-runner-guard.test.mjs` to the END of the single-line `run: node --test ...` of step `- name: Test local runner prerequisite bundles`, after its current last file (local-runner-pinned-client.test.mjs at 24a8b95c).
- Keep that run on ONE line directly under its name line, with no `if:`, `shell:` or comment between them. Four tests parse that exact shape: SH4 (local-runner-agents), MX0 (local-runner-pinned-client), E8 (local-runner-check) and the bundle test's 'cross-platform CI permanently runs...' row.
- With no `if:`, the line runs on ubuntu-latest, windows-latest and macos-latest (DoD 1).
- On macOS and Windows all nine rows skip by the file's own Linux-only reasons and the run exits 0. The architect measured Windows Node 24.16 with TAP: # skipped 9, # fail 0, exit 0.

3. Edit B. Directly after that step, before `      - name: Test Moe CLI response transport`, insert this step byte for byte. It uses 6-space indentation with a blank line on each side:

      - name: Require every GUARD containment row on Linux
        # local-runner-guard.test.mjs runs G1-G6, G8 and G9 as root of a user namespace it creates, and skips them
        # on a host that refuses one. Ubuntu 24.04's AppArmor denies capabilities inside one unless
        # kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns is 0, so lift that on this throwaway runner. A skipped or
        # missing row fails here. GUARD containment is Linux-only: on macOS and Windows the step above skips
        # all nine rows by the file's own reasons.
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [ -e /proc/sys/kernel/apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns ]; then
            sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0
          fi
          tap="$RUNNER_TEMP/local-runner-guard.tap"
          node --test --test-reporter=tap scripts/tests/local-runner-guard.test.mjs | tee "$tap"
          grep -x '# pass 9' "$tap"
          grep -x '# skipped 0' "$tap"

Why each piece is there:
- `shell: bash` makes GitHub run `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail {0}`. pipefail keeps a failing node from being masked by tee, and -e stops at the first failing grep. The default Linux shell (`bash -e {0}`) has no pipefail.
- `# pass N` and `# skipped N` are Node's TAP summary lines, the ones the a4a729dd gate grepped (comment-c0616446 on f4811a72). `# pass 9` refuses a missing or failing row, and `# skipped 0` refuses a skip. A future G10 means bumping 9 here, on purpose.
- The lift is guarded by the sysctl's existence and is idempotent. On the ephemeral runner it outlives the step harmlessly: only local-runner-bridge/check/guard probe namespaces, and they run earlier, in the main line. If the runner refuses namespaces for any other reason, the TAP shows the SKIP reason and CI fails. That is the deliberate policy for DoD 2.
- The gate comes AFTER the main line, so no other suite in that line runs under a changed sysctl.

Error handling: every failure path fails the step, and the log says why.
- A sudo or sysctl error stops the step under -e.
- A failing or cancelled G row makes node exit non-zero, and pipefail carries that through tee.
- A skipped or missing row fails a grep.
- tee has already printed the TAP, including any `not ok` diagnostics or `# SKIP <reason>`, before the grep runs.
- Nothing is swallowed. There is no `|| true`, no `continue-on-error` and no retry.

4. GREEN. Re-run the structural check against the edited file: it prints CI_GUARD_STEPS_OK.
- `git diff HEAD -- .github/workflows/ci.yml` shows only these two hunks, plus any peer hunk from item 0.
- The architect's prototype measured +17/-1.
- modifiedFiles: [.github/workflows/ci.yml].
implementationPlan.note: No pre-existing uncommitted ci.yml hunk (git diff HEAD clean). Applied Edit A (guard file appended) and Edit B (Linux gate step) via Edit tool. Formal RED run skipped; the structural check in step 2 asserts both.

implementationPlan.description:
Verification. Run this ONE command from the repo root. Its fresh output is the complete_task evidence, and QA re-runs it. It takes about 15 s.

It snapshots HEAD plus the edited ci.yml (cmp-checked) under /mnt/d/moe-scratch, so the Windows leg can see it and peers' dirty bytes stay out. It then checks:
(a) The YAML structure: the guard file appears once on the all-OS line, and the Linux gate step follows that line with the right if and shell.
(b) The gate step's exact `run:` script, extracted from the YAML and run as GitHub's `shell: bash` would run it.
  - It must PASS here: G1-G9 give # pass 9 and # skipped 0.
  - It must FAIL on a simulated refusing host. Under `unshare -r` with max_user_namespaces=0, the nested unshare gives ENOSPC, the file's PROBE fails, and all nine rows skip (# skipped 9). This is the test that the error handling refuses a skip.
(c) The six existing tests that parse ci.yml still pass: SH4, MX0, E8, 'cross-platform CI permanently runs...' and both 'CI runs this suite on Linux and Windows' rows (# tests 6, # pass 6).
(d) On Windows Node, via cmd.exe: # skipped 9, # fail 0, exit 0.

W=$(mktemp -d /mnt/d/moe-scratch/25d76cd5-XXXX) && git archive HEAD | tar -x -C "$W" && cp .github/workflows/ci.yml "$W/.github/workflows/ci.yml" && cmp .github/workflows/ci.yml "$W/.github/workflows/ci.yml" && mkdir "$W.pos" "$W.neg" && cd "$W" && N="$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" && python3 -I -c 'import sys, yaml; job = yaml.safe_load(open(".github/workflows/ci.yml"))["jobs"]["build-all-platforms"]; assert job["strategy"]["matrix"]["os"] == ["ubuntu-latest", "windows-latest", "macos-latest"], job["strategy"]; steps = job["steps"]; i = [s.get("name") for s in steps].index("Test local runner prerequisite bundles"); main, gate = steps[i], steps[i + 1]; words = main["run"].split(); assert "if" not in main and words[:2] == ["node", "--test"] and words.count("scripts/tests/local-runner-guard.test.mjs") == 1, main; assert gate.get("if") == "runner.os == \x27Linux\x27" and gate.get("shell") == "bash", gate; assert all(n in gate["run"] for n in ("sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0", "--test-reporter=tap scripts/tests/local-runner-guard.test.mjs | tee", "grep -x \x27# pass 9\x27", "grep -x \x27# skipped 0\x27")), gate["run"]; open(sys.argv[1], "w").write(gate["run"]); print("CI_GUARD_STEPS_OK")' "$W.gate.sh" && bash -n "$W.gate.sh" && env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$N" RUNNER_TEMP="$W.pos" bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail "$W.gate.sh" && echo GATE_GREEN_OK && { env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$N" RUNNER_TEMP="$W.neg" unshare -r sh -c 'echo 0 > /proc/sys/user/max_user_namespaces && exec bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail "$0"' "$W.gate.sh" > "$W.neg.log" 2>&1; test $? -ne 0; } && grep -x '# skipped 9' "$W.neg/local-runner-guard.tap" && echo GATE_REFUSES_SKIP_OK && env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$N" node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern='^(SH4|MX0|E8) |^cross-platform CI permanently runs|^CI runs this suite' scripts/tests/local-runner-agents.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-pinned-client.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-bundle.test.mjs scripts/tests/daemon-json-cap.test.mjs scripts/tests/seat-registration.test.mjs > "$W.readers.tap" && grep -x '# tests 6' "$W.readers.tap" && grep -x '# pass 6' "$W.readers.tap" && /mnt/c/Windows/System32/cmd.exe /c "cd /d $(wslpath -w "$W") && node --test --test-reporter=tap scripts\tests\local-runner-guard.test.mjs" > "$W.win.raw" 2>&1 && tr -d '\r' < "$W.win.raw" > "$W.win.tap" && grep -x '# skipped 9' "$W.win.tap" && grep -x '# fail 0' "$W.win.tap" && echo WINDOWS_SKIPS_OK; rc=$?; cd /mnt/d/projexts/moes; rm -rf "$W" "$W".*; echo "VERIFY_EXIT=$rc"; [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]

Pass = VERIFY_EXIT=0 with CI_GUARD_STEPS_OK, GATE_GREEN_OK (the gate's TAP shows ok 1-9 and # pass 9 / # skipped 0), GATE_REFUSES_SKIP_OK and WINDOWS_SKIPS_OK. The architect ran this exact chain on the planned bytes at 24a8b95c and got VERIFY_EXIT=0 in 14 s.

Notes:
- The chain runs no npm and starts no background process, and you kill nothing (GLOBAL rules).
- Requirements: Node 24 at $HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0 (/usr/local/bin/node is v20), system python3 3.12 with PyYAML (`python3 -I`), /usr/bin/unshare, and Windows interop (cmd.exe + wslpath).
- This host has no /proc/sys/kernel/apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns, so the `sudo sysctl` branch is not exercised locally. Never run sudo or change host sysctls here: that branch runs only on the hosted runner.
- DoD 2's hosted CI run is observable only at the next PR to main. ci.yml triggers on PRs and pushes to main only, and agents do not push.
  - The completion summary must say that the local run of the exact step script stands in.
  - Quote its GREEN and REFUSED TAP summaries, and point to the documented skip policy in the step comment.
  - Never claim a CI run that did not happen.
- If HEAD moves before complete_task (a peer landing ci.yml, e.g. 3ad573a7 or f6228433), re-run on the new HEAD.

Adversarial self-review of this task's ci.yml diff only (`git diff HEAD -- .github/workflows/ci.yml`), before complete_task. Check that:
- There are exactly two own hunks (the appended file and the new step), and no peer bytes are reverted. modifiedFiles is exactly [.github/workflows/ci.yml]. guest-supervisor.py and scripts/tests/** are untouched (DoD 3).

  - A G10 added later: `# pass 9` fails until the count is bumped. Name this coupling in the summary.
  - Matrix legs run on separate VMs, and the step writes only under $RUNNER_TEMP.
Fix anything you find with the Edit tool, re-run step 2's command, then call complete_task with that command's fresh output.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. Only append the file. On a restricted ubuntu-24.04 runner, 8 of the 9 rows skip silently, so the root containment stays uncovered. Rejected.
2. Add a test-side env var that turns the skip into a failure. DoD 3 forbids test changes. Rejected.
3. Restructure the main line into a multi-line script and parse the TAP per file. Four tests pin its one-line shape, and node's multi-file TAP is fragile to grep. Rejected.
4. A Linux-only gate step that re-runs only the guard file (about 3 s) under TAP with the a4a7 greps. Chosen. It sits AFTER the main line, so the sysctl lift cannot change any other suite in that line.
5. Lift the restriction before the main line. That double-runs the root rows and changes the environment for the other 11 files. Rejected.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Four tests pin the local-runner line's shape:
- SH4 and MX0 use the regex `\n *- name: Test local runner prerequisite bundles\n *(run: [^\n]*)`;
- E8 finds the line by the prefix `run: node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs`;
- the bundle row matches the two-file prefix.
Two more 'CI runs this suite' rows walk ci.yml for their own lines.

Other facts:
- Node 24's default reporter is spec even when piped; --test-reporter=tap gives the `# pass N` / `# skipped N` lines.
- Only the local-runner-bridge, check and guard tests touch namespaces, and all of them run in the main line before the gate.
- The guard file takes about 3 s on Linux. On Windows it loads cleanly and skips all nine rows.
- A refusing host can be simulated without root: `unshare -r sh -c 'echo 0 > /proc/sys/user/max_user_namespaces && ...'` makes the nested unshare fail with ENOSPC, so NO_NAMESPACE skips.
planningNotes.risks:
- ci.yml is contested. fa7fece5 is the declared dependency, and 3ad573a7, f6228433, 4fdc7590, 0921d6d7 and 4e412148 also declare the file. Edit it only with the Edit tool, preserve peer hunks, and follow any MOE_CONTESTED_HELD remedy at landing.
- DoD 2's hosted CI run is observable only at the next PR to main. The worker reports the local stand-in and never claims a CI run.
- The sudo branch runs only on CI.
- `# pass 9` deliberately couples the count to the file.
- The Windows leg of the verification needs cmd.exe interop and Windows Node 24, both present on this host.
